taxonomy.note: The holotype from Egypt, described by Stromer, was destroyed in the Second World War; a partial skeleton from the Kem Kem Group of Morocco (FSAC-KK 11888) was designated as the neotype.

diet.note: Fish-eating is widely accepted, and it may also have eaten other animals. How it caught fish is disputed: one team argues it was a semi-aquatic or aquatic animal that swam with its tail and hunted underwater (Ibrahim et al. 2014, 2020; Fabbri et al. 2022); others argue it was buoyant, could not dive, walked on two legs on land and fed by wading in shallow water (Henderson 2018; Sereno et al. 2022). Posture is debated with it: the aquatic hypothesis implies a quadrupedal stance on land, while Sereno et al. 2022 found it was bipedal.

timeRange.note: Sereno et al. 2022 place S. aegyptiacus in the Cenomanian (about 95 Ma); the Ma values are the ICS v2024/12 Cenomanian stage boundaries. Some PBDB occurrences from Morocco are only dated to Late Albian-Early Cenomanian, and a few Tunisian and Algerian referrals extend to the Aptian-Albian; these are not used here. NHM gives 99-94 Ma.

lengthM.note: Sereno et al. 2022 reconstruct an adult at just under 14 m; Henderson 2018 built a 15.55 m model following the Ibrahim et al. 2014 reconstruction, which those authors described as over 15 m long.

massKg.note: Volumetric (digital model) estimates: 6,500 kg (Henderson 2018) and 7,390 kg (Sereno et al. 2022, with bird-like air spaces; up to about 8,000 kg with less air space). Estimates depend on the reconstruction used.

text.en: Spinosaurus was one of the longest meat-eating dinosaurs known, about 14 to 15 metres long, living in North Africa roughly 100 to 94 million years ago. It had a long, narrow snout with cone-shaped teeth for catching fish, and a tall sail on its back. Scientists still argue about how it lived: was it a swimmer that chased fish underwater, or a wader that stood in the shallows and ambushed them?
The first Spinosaurus bones, found in Egypt in 1912, were destroyed during the Second World War. For decades scientists had only drawings and photographs to study.

alt.en: Cast of the Spinosaurus specimen FSAC-KK-11888 at the Field Museum in Chicago, mounted in a swimming posture that reflects one debated view of how it lived.

uncertain.note: Fish-eating is agreed, but whether Spinosaurus hunted underwater or waded is disputed (Ibrahim et al. 2014, 2020; Fabbri et al. 2022 vs Henderson 2018; Sereno et al. 2022).
Length depends on the reconstruction: just under 14 m (Sereno et al. 2022) versus over 15 m (Ibrahim et al. 2014, as modelled by Henderson 2018).
